nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of INF-FeCuS
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol of Cu(NO₃)₂·3H₂O, 2 mmol of Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O and 4 mmol of L-cysteine were stirred well in water (60 ml), and then the solution was removed into a sealed Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave (as seen in Fig. 1a). The iron-nickel foam (INF, 1×4 cm²) was soaked in the above solution and hydrothermally treated at 160°C for 6 h. Finally, the resulting sample was rinsed several times with deionized water and anhydrous ethanol and dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 6 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: INF-FeCuS consists of Fe0.95S1.05 (PDF#01-075-0600) and Cu7S4 (PDF#97-001-6011) phases with 53.6% Cu7S4 and 21.1% Fe0.95S1.05; INF-FeCu contains Fe3O4 (PDF#01-075-0449) and Cu2O (PDF#97-003-1057) with 58.3% Cu2O and 28.0% Fe3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As can be seen from the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of INF-FeCuS and INF-FeCu (Fig. 1b-c), INF-FeCu contains Fe3O4 (PDF#01-075-0449) and Cu2O (PDF#97-003-1057) phases, while INF-FeCuS consists of Fe0.95S1.05 (PDF#01-075-0600) and Cu7S4 (PDF#97-001-6011) phases ... the percentages of Cu7S4 and Fe0.95S1.05 in INF-FeCuS are 53.6% and 21.1%, respectively.

properties.description: X-ray diffraction pattern with multiple phases

nodes.characterization_summary: INF-FeCu shows larger-size tetrahedral particles (~10 μm) grown on INF surface; INF-FeCuS corresponds to knitting wool ball-like morphology with nanorods intertwined and tremella-like nanosheets on nanorod surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As seen from scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images, the morphologies of INF-FeCuS and INF-FeCu are obviously different. INF-FeCu shows the larger-size tetrahedral particles (~10 μm) grown on the INF surface (Fig. 1d-f) ... INF-FeCuS corresponds to the knitting wool ball-like morphology with many nanorods intertwined with each other, while some tremella-like nanosheets grows on the nanorod surface (Fig. 1g-i).

nodes.characterization_summary: INF-FeCuS shows nanorod structure with rough surface and ultrathin nanosheets; lattice spacings of 0.205 nm (Fe0.95S1.05 (102)) and 0.195 nm (Cu7S4 (224)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscope (TEM) image of INF-FeCuS shows a nanorod structure with a rough surface. Some ultrathin nano-sheets can be found grown on the surface of these nanorods (Fig. 2a). From high-resolution TEM (HRTEM), the lattice spacings of nanorod and nanosheet in INF-FeCuS are 0.205 nm and 0.195 nm (Fig. 2b), which correspond to the (102) and (224) crystal planes of Fe0.95S1.05 and Cu7S4, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED demonstrates existence of (102) Fe0.95S1.05 and (224) Cu7S4 crystal planes in INF-FeCuS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) also demonstrates the existence of (102) and (224) crystal planes (Fig. 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Cu, S, and Fe in INF-FeCuS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental distributions from INF-FeCuS (Fig. 2d) shows the uniform distribution Cu, S and Fe in INF-FeCuS.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area of INF-FeCuS is 17.78 m²/g, about twice that of INF-FeCu (9.09 m²/g); INF-FeCuS has more mesopores (3-6 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As showed in the N2 adsorption and desorption curve (Fig. S4a), the BET specific surface area of INF-FeCuS is 17.78 m² g⁻¹, which is about twice that of INF-FeCu (9.09 m² g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of INF-FeCuS shows Cu 2p with Cu(I) (932.4/952.2 eV, 73%) and Cu(II) (933.0/952.8 eV), Fe 2p with Fe(III)/Fe(II) ratio 0.78 (Fe(III): 714.0/726.8 eV, Fe(II): 711.3/724.4 eV), S 2p with S²⁻ (161.8/163.0 eV); INF-FeCu shows lower Cu(I) content and Fe(III)/Fe(II) ratio 0.58.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Specially, in the Cu 2p spectrum of INF-FeCuS (Fig. 2e), the Cu (I) 2p3/2 and Cu(I) 2p1/2 spin orbitals are located at 932.4 eV and 952.2 eV, while the peaks at 933.0 eV and 952.8 eV are attributed to Cu(II) 2p3/2 and Cu(II) 2p1/2 ... the content of Cu¹⁺ in INF-FeCuS is 73% being much higher than that in INF-FeCu ... INF-FeCuS shows much higher Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ ratio (0.78), comparing with that of INF-FeCu (0.58) ... The spin-orbit double peaks at 161.8 eV and 163.0 eV in the S 2p spectrum (Fig. 2g) can be attributed to S²⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV tests show electrochemical double-layer capacitance Cdl of INF-FeCuS is 31.2 mF/cm², indicating large electrochemically active surface area (ECSA).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, we perform cyclic voltammetry (CV) tests in 1 M KOH solution with different scan rates to obtain the value of the electrochemical double-layer capacitances (Cdl) of the sample (Fig. S6c-f). The Cdl value of INF-FeCuS is as large as 31.2 mF cm⁻² (Fig. S6c), illustrating that INF-FeCuS has a large the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA).
